cells.tense: You are in the middle of an ending that feels genuinely finished, and you are letting it end without a fight.
cells.ask: Let one person in on how you know something is complete — say what told you, not only what changed.
cells.core: The endings in your life are happening because they need to, not because you forced or avoided them. You can feel when something is done, and you let it be done — cleanly, without dragging it behind you or pushing it away too early. That quiet knowing is not a mood. It is the capacity to tell finished from unfinished, and it is one of the most load-bearing things you have.\n\nBecause the release is running, it can now carry more than one life. Let someone in on how you decide. What they get is not an opinion on your choices — it is the first time they hear permission to end something of their own.
cells.sheetLine: You know when something is done, and you let it be done.
cells.verb: let what is finished fall away so what comes next has room to arrive
cells.place: in the part of a life that knows how to let go on purpose

cells.tense: You are already living past the next ending — rehearsing the clearing before the thing has actually stopped.
cells.ask: Let one person feel the weight of what they are carrying before you suggest they put it down.
cells.core: Something in you has decided that endings are the only safe move, so you are making them everywhere — walking out of rooms that haven't finished, cutting ties that still have thread, calling the leaving freedom when it is really the next leaving already on your face. The clearing is real, but it has outrun the thing it was clearing.\n\nBefore you end anything today, take a minute to stand beside whoever is in it with you. Not to save them. Not to fix it. Just to feel what they feel from inside their position instead of watching from the exit. The ending that follows will be yours, not the fear's.
cells.sheetLine: You are ending things faster than they can finish.

cells.tense: You are standing at a doorway that already closed behind you, still holding the handle from the other side.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have been carrying past its need, and let a small piece of it go today — not the whole load, just one corner of it.
cells.core: You are loyal to things past their time — a role, a habit, an old arrangement — and you call it staying true. But it is not faithfulness you are feeling. It is the grip that never got told to open. Letting go feels like abandoning something, so nothing gets released, and the space where the next thing would land stays full of what came before.\n\nYou do not need to feel like letting go in order to do it. Pick the smallest thing. Put one corner of it down today, just to feel your hands move. You are not deciding what your life means. You are only moving, and movement from a true place has its own direction.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding on to something that has already let go of you.

cells.place: in the part of a life that knows how to let go on purpose

cells.tense: An ending is already underway in you, and you have been describing it to yourself as a bad spell or a busy week.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, one thing you are already letting go of, without explaining why it matters or defending the decision.
cells.core: Something is shifting in you right now — a role loosening, a preference going quiet, an old way of being yourself that no longer fits — and you are not naming it, so it reads as chaos from inside. You feel the change without understanding what it is changing, and you keep trying to put the pieces back the way they were.\n\nBefore you fix anything, name one small piece of what is going. Say it plainly — to a person, to a page, to the room. Not to make it official. To hand yourself back the pen. The structure that holds you up does not come from outside you. It is one thing you can put words to, today.
cells.sheetLine: Something in you is ending, and you are calling it a rough patch.
